newsitem.title: USA: SEC agrees to settle with Maricopa County, Ariz..
newsitem.headline: SEC agrees to settle with Maricopa County, Ariz..

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday it has agreed to settle securities fraud charges against Maricopa County, Ariz., marking the formal close of its proceedings against the county.

Under the settlement, announced by the SEC's office in Los Angeles, the county agreed to cease and desist from current and future violations of the anti-fraud provisions of federal securities laws but neither admitted nor denied any of the SEC's allegations. No fines or penalties were imposed.
Maricopa County's supervisors approved the settlement at a meeting in Phoenix, Ariz., on Wednesday.

Earlier this week, the SEC alleged that Maricopa County, the nation's sixth largest county, violated the anti-fraud provisions of federal securities laws in connection with the July 1993 sale of two series of general obligation bonds by failing to disclose that county finances had deteriorated.

The SEC action against Maricopa County was precedent setting because it was the first action by the commission against a general purpose issuer of municipal bonds where the securities were not in default.
The Maricopa County case was also the first major SEC action in the municipal bond market since its settlement with then-bankrupt Orange County, Calif., in January.
In a related announcement on Wednesday, SEC officials in Los Angeles said they settled securities fraud charges against financial adviser Peacock, Hislop, Staley & Given Inc. over the county bonds.

As part of that settlement, the Phoenix-based firm agreed to pay $50,000 in fines and partner Larry Given agreed to $25,000 in fines for their involvement in the bond deals. Under the terms of the deal, the firm neither admitted nor denied any of the SEC's findings.
